newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cash problems delay mission to Mir space station.
newsitem.headline: Cash problems delay mission to Mir space station.

text.p: Cash problems have forced the postponement of a German-Russian mission to replace the three-man crew on the space station Mir, Itar-Tass news agency said on Thursday.
Tass quoted officials at the Flight Control Centre outside Moscow as saying the launch scheduled for December 15 had been put back to February.
Financial problems had forced a sharp cutback in the production of the booster rockets needed for such launches and none was available, it said.

German astronaut Reinhold Ewald had been due to travel with Russians Alexander Lazutkin and Vasily Tsibliyev to replace a three-man Russian-American crew on Mir, indicating that the current crew now faces a longer stay in space than planned.
"Ewald will not yet achieve his dream of celebrating Christmas and New Year in space," Tass said.
U.S. astronaut John Blaha and his two Russian colleagues, Valery Korzun and Alexander Kolery, have been on the 10-year-old station since September 19.
Tass did not set a date for their return to earth and Russian space officials were not immediately available for comment due to the national holiday on Thursday.
It was yet another blow for Russia's space programme, which has been dogged by financial problems since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.
The flights of at least four unmanned supply ships have been cancelled this year because of cash problems.
Interfax news agency said on Wednesday that the two Russians and one American on Mir also had toilet trouble.
Containers holding their bodily waste fluids were filling up fast and replacements were not due for weeks, it quoted unidentified sources as saying.
The agency said a device which recycles the crew's waste into the craft's cooling system had broken down and all the reserve containers were nearly full.
The crew could also not find the pump used to transfer the waste water into the cooling system, it added.
New waste containers were due to be shipped out in October but financial problems had meant the supply ship was not able to leave and was not due to be launched until November 20.
